clinicalPearls: Retractile mesenteritis represents the fibrotic, end-stage variant of a spectrum of idiopathic mesenteric inflammation; the earlier fat-predominant form is termed mesenteric panniculitis and the fat-necrosis-predominant form mesenteric lipodystrophy.
It preferentially involves the root of the small-bowel mesentery, typically sparing the retroperitoneum, and shows a striking male predominance in later middle age.
Presentation is often insidious with vague abdominal pain, a palpable mass, altered bowel habit, weight loss or a low-grade febrile illness, though some cases are found incidentally on imaging.

CT is the pivotal investigation: a soft-tissue mesenteric mass with the 'fat-ring sign' (preserved fat halo around vessels and nodes) and a hyperattenuating 'tumoural pseudocapsule' are characteristic.
The retractile subtype is defined by dense collagenous fibrosis that tethers and kinks bowel loops, producing bowel obstruction, ischaemia or venous/lymphatic compromise.
An association with IgG4-related disease, prior abdominal surgery or trauma, and occult malignancy (notably lymphoma) is recognised, mandating a search for an underlying cause.

Diagnosis is one of exclusion confirmed histologically, showing fat necrosis, chronic inflammation and mature fibrosis; the fibrotic burden distinguishes retractile mesenteritis from milder panniculitis.

Management is guided by symptom severity: asymptomatic disease is observed, while symptomatic or progressive fibrosis is treated with immunosuppression, with surgery reserved for obstructive complications.
reference.pathophysiology: Retractile mesenteritis is an idiopathic, chronic non-neoplastic disorder characterised by a self-limiting or progressive inflammatory-fibrotic process centred on the adipose tissue of the mesentery, most often the small-bowel mesenteric root. It is conceptualised as the sclerotic end of a continuum that begins with mesenteric panniculitis (chronic inflammation of mesenteric fat), passes through mesenteric lipodystrophy (predominant fat necrosis with foamy macrophage infiltration), and culminates in the retractile form dominated by dense collagen deposition. The initiating insult is uncertain, but proposed triggers include prior abdominal surgery or trauma, mesenteric ischaemia, autoimmunity and a paraneoplastic response; a subset falls within the IgG4-related disease spectrum, showing storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis and IgG4-rich plasma-cell infiltrates. As the process matures, myofibroblast proliferation and progressive collagenisation cause tissue contraction that retracts and tethers the mesentery, kinking bowel loops and encasing mesenteric vessels, lymphatics and nodes. This retraction underlies the clinical hallmarks of bowel obstruction, protein-losing enteropathy, chylous ascites and, occasionally, bowel or vascular ischaemia from encasement of the superior mesenteric vessels.
additionalDifferentials: Mesenteric lymphoma or other lymphoproliferative disease
Carcinoid tumour with desmoplastic mesenteric reaction
Peritoneal carcinomatosis or desmoplastic metastatic deposits
Mesenteric tuberculosis or other granulomatous mesenteric infection
IgG4-related sclerosing disease at other sites
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen to assess the fat-ring sign, pseudocapsule and vascular encasement
MRI to characterise the degree of fibrosis versus active inflammation
Image-guided or surgical biopsy for histological confirmation and exclusion of malignancy
Serum IgG4 subclass and immunoglobulin profile to assess for IgG4-related disease
Inflammatory markers and full blood count to gauge systemic inflammatory activity
18F-FDG PET to evaluate metabolic activity and screen for underlying lymphoma or malignancy
Nutritional and protein assessment where protein-losing enteropathy or chylous ascites is suspected
redFlags: Features of bowel obstruction or mesenteric ischaemia from fibrotic bowel tethering or vascular encasement
Rapid mass enlargement, lymphadenopathy or constitutional symptoms suggesting underlying lymphoma or malignancy
Development of chylous ascites or protein-losing enteropathy indicating lymphatic compromise
Signs of superior mesenteric vein thrombosis or bowel infarction
Systemic multi-site sclerosis suggesting progressive IgG4-related disease
reference.prognosis: Most cases follow a benign, indolent or self-limiting course, and asymptomatic disease often remains stable or regresses on surveillance. The retractile fibrotic subtype carries a less favourable outlook because progressive contraction can cause bowel obstruction, ischaemia and nutritional compromise, though survival remains good when an underlying malignancy is excluded.
pitfalls: Mistaking the CT appearance for lymphoma or carcinomatosis and either over-treating or delaying appropriate biopsy
Attributing all mesenteric fat stranding to mesenteritis when it reflects incidental panniculitis or an adjacent inflammatory process
Failing to search for occult malignancy, particularly lymphoma, which can present with an identical desmoplastic mesenteric reaction
Overlooking an IgG4-related aetiology that would respond to targeted immunosuppression
Proceeding to extensive resection when the tethered mesentery renders surgery hazardous and symptoms could be managed medically
references: Standard gastroenterology and abdominal imaging references
management: Reserve treatment for symptomatic or progressive disease and manage the active inflammatory phase with corticosteroids
Add steroid-sparing agents such as tamoxifen, azathioprine or colchicine for corticosteroid-refractory or relapsing fibrosis
Treat disease within the IgG4-related spectrum with corticosteroids, reserving rituximab for resistant cases
Manage asymptomatic, incidentally discovered disease with clinical and cross-sectional imaging surveillance
Reserve surgical bypass or resection for established bowel obstruction, ischaemia or intractable disease
Investigate for and exclude an underlying malignancy, particularly lymphoma, before labelling the disease idiopathic
Provide nutritional support and analgesia for weight loss and chronic abdominal pain
